cards.etymology: From Latin vertebra ‘joint (of the spine)’, from vertere ‘to turn’ — the bones on which the back turns. ‘Thoracic’ is from Greek thōrax ‘breastplate, chest’, so this is the eighth chest vertebra — the one that carries rib 8.
cards.tip: The inferior vena cava passes through the diaphragm at about the T8 level.

cards.name: T9 vertebra
cards.etymology: From Latin vertebra ‘joint (of the spine)’, from vertere ‘to turn’ — the bones on which the back turns. ‘Thoracic’ is from Greek thōrax ‘breastplate, chest’, so this is the ninth chest vertebra — the one that carries rib 9.
landmarks: Inferior demifacet for rib 10 often small or absent
cards.tip: The xiphisternal joint lies at about the T9 level.

cards.name: Trapezium
cards.etymology: From Greek trapezion ‘little table’ (a four-sided figure). So it means ‘the little table bone’ — irregular and four-sided. Remember: trapeziUM is by the thUMb. Carpal is from Greek karpos ‘wrist’.
landmarks: Groove for the flexor carpi radialis tendon
cards.tip: Its saddle joint with the 1st metacarpal gives the thumb opposition — and is a classic site of osteoarthritis.

cards.name: Trapezoid
cards.etymology: From Greek trapezoeidēs ‘table-shaped’ (trapeza ‘table’ + -oeidēs ‘like’). So it means ‘shaped like a little table’ — a small wedge-like four-sided bone. Carpal is from Greek karpos ‘wrist’.
landmarks: Smallest bone of the distal row
Fits into the notched base of the 2nd metacarpal
cards.tip: Locks into the forked base of the 2nd metacarpal, making the index ray the stable ‘fixed’ unit of the hand.

cards.name: Triquetrum
cards.etymology: From Latin triquetrus ‘three-cornered, triangular’. So it means ‘the triangular bone’ — pyramid-shaped. Carpal is from Greek karpos ‘wrist’.
landmarks: Oval facet for the pisiform on its palmar surface
cards.tip: The second most commonly fractured carpal — typically a dorsal chip from a fall onto the back of the hand.

cards.name: Abductor digiti minimi (foot)
cards.etymology: From Latin abducere ‘to lead away’ + digiti ‘of the digit’ + minimi ‘smallest’. So it means ‘the muscle that draws the little toe away’ from the others.
cards.origin: Medial and lateral processes of the calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis
cards.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th toe
actions: 5th toe flexion at the MTP joint
cards.tip: Forms the lateral border of the sole.

cards.name: Abductor digiti minimi (hand)
cards.etymology: From Latin abductor ‘one that leads away’ + digiti minimi ‘of the smallest finger’. So it means ‘the muscle that leads the little finger away’.
cards.origin: Pisiform and tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris (pisohamate ligament)
cards.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th digit
cards.tip: The most superficial and medial hypothenar muscle — its wasting is an early sign of ulnar neuropathy.

cards.name: Abductor hallucis
cards.etymology: From Latin abducere ‘to lead away’ (ab ‘away’ + ducere ‘to lead’) + hallucis ‘of the big toe’. So it means ‘the muscle that draws the big toe away’ from the second toe.
cards.origin: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity, flexor retinaculum and plantar aponeurosis
cards.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe
actions: Great toe flexion at the MTP joint
cards.tip: Forms the medial border of the sole; a key ‘short foot’ exercise target for arch control and bunion management.

cards.name: Abductor pollicis brevis
cards.etymology: From Latin abductor ‘one that leads away’ + pollicis ‘of the thumb’ + brevis ‘short’. So it means ‘the short muscle that leads the thumb away’.
cards.origin: Flexor retinaculum and the tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium
cards.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
cards.tip: The most superficial thenar muscle — weakness and wasting here is a classic sign of advanced carpal tunnel syndrome.

cards.name: Abductor pollicis longus
cards.etymology: From Latin abductor ‘one that leads away’ (ab ‘away’ + ducere ‘to lead’) + pollicis ‘of the thumb’ + longus ‘long’. So it means ‘the long muscle that leads the thumb away’.
cards.origin: Posterior surfaces of the proximal halves of ulna and radius and the interosseous membrane
cards.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the 1st metacarpal
actions: Thumb abduction at the CMC joint
Thumb extension at the CMC joint
cards.innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, deep branch of radial (C7–C8)
cards.tip: With EPB it forms the first dorsal compartment — inflamed in De Quervain’s tenosynovitis (Finkelstein test); the pair bounds the anatomical snuffbox radially.

cards.name: Adductor hallucis
cards.etymology: From Latin adducere ‘to lead towards’ + hallucis ‘of the big toe’. So it means ‘the muscle that draws the big toe in’ toward the second toe — it has oblique and transverse heads.
cards.origin: Oblique head: bases of metatarsals 2–4; transverse head: plantar ligaments of MTP joints 3–5
cards.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe (via the lateral sesamoid)
actions: Great toe flexion at the MTP joint
cards.innervation: Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3)
cards.tip: Its unopposed pull contributes to hallux valgus (bunion) deformity.

cards.name: Adductor pollicis
cards.etymology: From Latin adductor ‘one that leads toward’ (ad ‘toward’ + ducere ‘to lead’) + pollicis ‘of the thumb’. So it means ‘the muscle that draws the thumb toward the palm’.
cards.origin: Oblique head: bases of 2nd and 3rd metacarpals, capitate and adjacent carpals; transverse head: anterior surface of the shaft of the 3rd metacarpal
cards.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb (via the ulnar sesamoid)
cards.tip: Ulnar nerve palsy weakens it — Froment’s sign: the patient flexes the thumb IP (using FPL) to hold paper in a key pinch.

cards.name: Anconeus
cards.etymology: From Greek ankōn ‘elbow’ (via Latin anconeus). So it means ‘the elbow muscle’.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle of humerus
cards.insertion: Lateral surface of the olecranon and superior part of the posterior surface of ulna
cards.tip: A small triangular extension of the triceps; it tensions the posterolateral capsule and helps stabilise the elbow.

cards.name: Coccygeus
cards.etymology: From Greek kokkyx ‘cuckoo’ — the coccyx resembles a cuckoo’s beak. So it means ‘the coccyx muscle’; the alternative name ischiococcygeus says it runs ischium to coccyx.
cards.origin: Ischial spine and sacrospinous ligament
cards.insertion: Lateral margins of lower sacrum and coccyx
cards.tip: Lies on the deep surface of the sacrospinous ligament; can refer pain in coccydynia.

cards.name: Digastric
cards.etymology: From Greek di- ‘two’ + gastēr ‘belly’. So it means ‘two-bellied’ — anterior and posterior bellies joined by an intermediate tendon.
cards.origin: Anterior belly: digastric fossa of mandible; posterior belly: mastoid notch of temporal bone
cards.insertion: Intermediate tendon, held to body and greater horn of hyoid by a fibrous sling
actions: Depresses mandible (mouth opening, esp. against resistance)
cards.innervation: Anterior belly: nerve to mylohyoid (CN V3); posterior belly: facial nerve (CN VII)
cards.tip: Two bellies, two embryonic origins, two nerves — a favourite exam question.

cards.name: Dorsal interossei (foot)
cards.etymology: From Latin dorsalis ‘of the back’ + inter ‘between’ + ossa ‘bones’. So it means ‘the muscles between the bones, on the back (top) side’ — four bipennate muscles between the metatarsals.
cards.origin: Adjacent sides of metatarsals 1–5 (two heads each)
cards.insertion: Bases of the proximal phalanges and extensor expansions: 1st to medial side of 2nd toe, 2nd–4th to lateral sides of toes 2–4
actions: Abduction of toes 2–4 (away from the axis through the 2nd toe)
cards.tip: ‘DAB’ — Dorsal ABduct; in the foot the reference line runs through the 2nd toe, not the 3rd as in the hand.

cards.name: Dorsal interossei of the hand
cards.etymology: From Latin dorsalis ‘of the back’ + inter ‘between’ + os/ossis ‘bone’. So it means ‘the muscles between the bones on the back of the hand’ (between the metacarpals).
cards.origin: Adjacent sides of the 1st–5th metacarpals (four bipennate muscles)
cards.insertion: Bases of the proximal phalanges and extensor expansions of digits 2–4 (radial side of 2nd and 3rd; ulnar side of 3rd and 4th)
actions: Finger abduction (digits 2–4, away from the axis of the middle finger)
cards.tip: Mnemonic DAB — Dorsal ABduct; the 1st dorsal interosseous is the bulge between thumb and index and wastes visibly in ulnar palsy.

cards.name: Extensor carpi radialis brevis
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘straightener’ + carpi ‘of the wrist’ + radialis ‘radial side’ + brevis ‘short’. So it means ‘the short radial wrist extensor’.
cards.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus (common extensor tendon)
cards.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the 3rd metacarpal
cards.tip: Its origin is the usual site of lateral epicondylalgia (tennis elbow) — progressive eccentric wrist-extension loading is first-line rehab.

cards.name: Extensor carpi radialis longus
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘stretcher, straightener’ + carpi ‘of the wrist’ + radialis ‘radial side’ + longus ‘long’. So it means ‘the long radial wrist extensor’.
cards.origin: Distal third of the lateral supracondylar ridge of humerus
cards.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the 2nd metacarpal
cards.tip: Works with ECRB to hold the wrist extended during gripping, giving the finger flexors optimal length.

cards.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘straightener’ + carpi ‘of the wrist’ + ulnaris ‘of the ulna (ulnar side)’. So it means ‘the wrist extensor on the ulnar side’.
cards.origin: Humeral head: lateral epicondyle (common extensor tendon); ulnar head: posterior border of ulna (by aponeurosis)
cards.insertion: Medial (dorsal) side of the base of the 5th metacarpal
cards.innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, deep branch of radial (C7–C8)
cards.tip: Its tendon can sublux over the ulnar head — a cause of ulnar-sided wrist pain in racquet and golf athletes.

cards.name: Extensor digiti minimi
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘straightener’ + digiti minimi ‘of the smallest finger’. So it means ‘the extensor of the little finger’.
cards.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus (common extensor tendon)
cards.insertion: Extensor expansion of the 5th digit
actions: Little finger MCP and IP extension
cards.innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, deep branch of radial (C7–C8)
cards.tip: Lets you extend the little finger independently — the “pinky out” muscle.

cards.name: Extensor digitorum
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘straightener’ + digitorum ‘of the fingers’. So it means ‘the extensor of the fingers’.
cards.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus (common extensor tendon)
cards.insertion: Extensor (dorsal digital) expansions of digits 2–5, to bases of middle and distal phalanges
actions: Finger IP extension (with lumbricals and interossei)
cards.innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, deep branch of radial (C7–C8)
cards.tip: Linked by intertendinous connections on the back of the hand — the reason it is hard to lift your ring finger alone.

cards.name: Extensor digitorum brevis
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘straightener’ + digitorum ‘of the digits’ + brevis ‘short’. So it means ‘the short extensor of the toes’ — a small muscle on top of the foot.
cards.origin: Superolateral surface of the calcaneus and inferior extensor retinaculum
cards.insertion: Lateral sides of the long extensor tendons of toes 2–4
cards.tip: The only muscle on the dorsum of the foot (with EHB) — the soft bulge in front of the lateral malleolus.

cards.name: Extensor digitorum longus
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘straightener’ + digitorum ‘of the digits’ + longus ‘long’. So it means ‘the long extensor of the toes’.
cards.origin: Lateral condyle of the tibia, upper three-quarters of the anterior fibula and interosseous membrane
cards.insertion: Middle and distal phalanges of toes 2–5 via the dorsal extensor expansions
cards.tip: Its four tendons fan out across the dorsum of the foot; it is the ‘Eating Disorder’ (Extensor Digitorum) in ‘Tom Has A Very Nervous Eating Disorder’.

cards.name: Extensor hallucis brevis
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘straightener’ + hallucis ‘of the big toe’ + brevis ‘short’. So it means ‘the short extensor of the big toe’.
cards.origin: Superolateral surface of the calcaneus (with extensor digitorum brevis)
cards.insertion: Dorsal base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe
actions: Great toe extension at the MTP joint
cards.tip: Essentially the medial slip of extensor digitorum brevis.

cards.name: Extensor hallucis longus
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘straightener’ + hallucis ‘of the big toe’ (hallux) + longus ‘long’. So it means ‘the long extensor of the big toe’.
cards.origin: Middle part of the anterior surface of the fibula and interosseous membrane
cards.insertion: Dorsal base of the distal phalanx of the great toe
cards.tip: Testing big-toe extension strength is a quick screen of the L5 myotome. It is the ‘H’ in ‘Tom Has A Very Nervous Eating Disorder’.

cards.name: Extensor indicis
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘straightener’ + indicis ‘of the pointer (index finger)’ (index, ‘one that points out’). So it means ‘the extensor of the pointing finger’.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of the distal third of the ulna and the interosseous membrane
cards.insertion: Extensor expansion of the index finger (ulnar side of the extensor digitorum tendon)
actions: Index finger MCP and IP extension (independent pointing)
cards.innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, deep branch of radial (C7–C8)
cards.tip: Gives the index finger independent extension — the “pointing” muscle; its tendon is sometimes transferred to replace a ruptured EPL.

cards.name: Extensor pollicis brevis
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘straightener’ + pollicis ‘of the thumb’ + brevis ‘short’. So it means ‘the short extensor of the thumb’.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of the distal third of the radius and the interosseous membrane
cards.insertion: Dorsal base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
cards.innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, deep branch of radial (C7–C8)
cards.tip: Shares the first dorsal compartment with APL (De Quervain’s); forms the radial border of the anatomical snuffbox.

cards.name: Extensor pollicis longus
cards.etymology: From Latin extensor ‘straightener’ + pollicis ‘of the thumb’ + longus ‘long’. So it means ‘the long extensor of the thumb’.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of the middle third of the ulna and the interosseous membrane
cards.insertion: Dorsal base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
actions: Thumb retroposition (lifts thumb off the table)
cards.innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, deep branch of radial (C7–C8)
cards.tip: Hooks around Lister’s tubercle and forms the ulnar border of the anatomical snuffbox; can rupture weeks after a distal radius fracture.

cards.name: External anal sphincter
cards.etymology: From Greek sphinkter ‘that which binds tight’ (sphingein, to bind) + Latin analis ‘of the anus’ (anus, ring) + externus ‘outer’. So it means ‘the outer tightening ring of the anus’.
cards.origin: Perineal body (anteriorly) and skin around anus
cards.insertion: Anococcygeal body and coccyx (posteriorly), encircling the anal canal
actions: Voluntary closure of anal canal (faecal continence)
cards.innervation: Inferior rectal nerve (pudendal, S2–S4) and perineal branch of S4
cards.tip: Voluntary skeletal muscle (unlike the internal sphincter); often injured in obstetric tears, so pelvic floor rehab may target it.

cards.name: Fibularis tertius
cards.etymology: From Latin fibula ‘clasp, brooch’ + -aris ‘relating to’ + tertius ‘third’. So it means ‘the third fibula muscle’ (peroneus is from Greek peronē ‘pin’, the same idea).
cards.origin: Lower third of the anterior surface of the fibula and interosseous membrane
cards.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the 5th metatarsal
cards.tip: Really a lower slip of extensor digitorum longus and absent in some people — unlike the other fibularis muscles it sits in the anterior compartment.

cards.name: Flexor carpi radialis
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + carpi ‘of the wrist’ (Greek karpos) + radialis ‘of the radius (radial side)’. So it means ‘the wrist flexor on the radial side’.
cards.origin: Medial epicondyle of humerus (common flexor tendon)
cards.insertion: Base of the 2nd metacarpal (and slip to the 3rd)
cards.tip: Its tendon is the landmark for the radial pulse (artery just lateral) — part of the common flexor origin stressed in medial epicondylalgia (golfer’s elbow).

cards.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + carpi ‘of the wrist’ + ulnaris ‘of the ulna (ulnar side)’. So it means ‘the wrist flexor on the ulnar side’.
cards.origin: Humeral head: medial epicondyle (common flexor tendon); ulnar head: medial margin of olecranon and proximal two-thirds of the posterior border of ulna
cards.insertion: Pisiform, then via pisohamate ligament to hook of hamate and pisometacarpal ligament to base of 5th metacarpal
cards.tip: The ulnar nerve enters the forearm between its two heads (cubital tunnel) — a site of entrapment; the only anterior forearm muscle fully supplied by the ulnar nerve besides the medial FDP.

cards.name: Flexor digiti minimi brevis (foot)
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + digiti ‘of the digit’ + minimi ‘smallest’. So it means ‘the flexor of the little toe’.
cards.origin: Base of the 5th metatarsal and sheath of the fibularis longus tendon
cards.insertion: Lateral base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th toe
actions: 5th toe flexion at the MTP joint
cards.innervation: Superficial branch of the lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3)
cards.tip: Lies alongside abductor digiti minimi in the lateral compartment of the sole.

cards.name: Flexor digiti minimi brevis (hand)
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + digiti minimi ‘of the smallest finger’ + brevis ‘short’. So it means ‘the short flexor of the little finger’.
cards.origin: Hook of hamate and flexor retinaculum
cards.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th digit
cards.tip: Part of the hypothenar eminence with ADM and opponens digiti minimi; often fused with ADM.

cards.name: Flexor digitorum brevis
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + digitorum ‘of the digits’ + brevis ‘short’. So it means ‘the short flexor of the toes’.
cards.origin: Medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis
cards.insertion: Both sides of the middle phalanges of toes 2–5
actions: Flexion of toes 2–5 at the PIP joints
cards.tip: Its split tendons let the FDL tendons pass through to the distal phalanges — like FDS in the hand.

cards.name: Flexor digitorum longus
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + digitorum ‘of the digits’ + longus ‘long’. So it means ‘the long flexor of the toes’.
cards.origin: Medial part of the posterior surface of the tibia below the soleal line
cards.insertion: Plantar bases of the distal phalanges of toes 2–5
cards.tip: The ‘Dick’ in ‘Tom, Dick And Very Nervous Harry’ behind the medial malleolus; quadratus plantae and the lumbricals attach to its tendons.

cards.name: Flexor digitorum profundus
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + digitorum ‘of the fingers’ + profundus ‘deep’. So it means ‘the deep finger flexor’.
cards.origin: Proximal three-quarters of the anterior and medial surfaces of ulna and adjacent interosseous membrane
cards.insertion: Bases of the distal phalanges of digits 2–5 (palmar surface)
cards.innervation: Medial part (digits 4–5): ulnar nerve (C8–T1); lateral part (digits 2–3): anterior interosseous branch of median nerve (C8–T1)
cards.tip: The only muscle that flexes the DIP joints; its tendons run through the carpal tunnel, and avulsion from the ring finger is “jersey finger”.

cards.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + digitorum ‘of the fingers’ (digitus) + superficialis ‘on the surface’. So it means ‘the superficial finger flexor’ (above flexor digitorum profundus).
cards.origin: Humero-ulnar head: medial epicondyle (common flexor tendon), ulnar collateral ligament and coronoid process of ulna; radial head: superior half of anterior border of radius (oblique line)
cards.insertion: Sides of the middle phalanges of digits 2–5 (each tendon splits around the FDP tendon)
cards.tip: Its four tendons pass through the carpal tunnel — test it by flexing one finger’s PIP while the others are held in extension.

cards.name: Flexor hallucis brevis
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + hallucis ‘of the big toe’ + brevis ‘short’. So it means ‘the short flexor of the big toe’ — it has medial and lateral heads.
cards.origin: Plantar surfaces of the cuboid and lateral cuneiform
cards.insertion: Both sides of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe (each head via a sesamoid bone)
actions: Great toe flexion at the MTP joint
cards.tip: Each head’s tendon contains a sesamoid under the 1st metatarsal head — irritation there is ‘sesamoiditis’.

cards.name: Flexor hallucis longus
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + hallucis ‘of the big toe’ + longus ‘long’. So it means ‘the long flexor of the big toe’.
cards.origin: Lower two-thirds of the posterior surface of the fibula and interosseous membrane
cards.insertion: Plantar base of the distal phalanx of the great toe
cards.tip: Key for push-off in walking and running (and dancers’ en pointe); the ‘Harry’ in ‘Tom, Dick And Very Nervous Harry’.

cards.name: Flexor pollicis brevis
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + pollicis ‘of the thumb’ + brevis ‘short’. So it means ‘the short flexor of the thumb’.
cards.origin: Superficial head: flexor retinaculum and tubercle of trapezium; deep head: trapezoid and capitate
cards.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb (via the radial sesamoid)
cards.innervation: Superficial head: recurrent branch of median nerve (C8–T1); deep head: deep branch of ulnar nerve (C8–T1)
cards.tip: Dual nerve supply means thumb flexion is often partly spared in an isolated median or ulnar nerve lesion.

cards.name: Flexor pollicis longus
cards.etymology: From Latin flexor ‘bender’ + pollicis ‘of the thumb’ (pollex) + longus ‘long’. So it means ‘the long flexor of the thumb’.
cards.origin: Anterior surface of the radius and adjacent interosseous membrane (variable slip from coronoid process/medial epicondyle)
cards.insertion: Palmar base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
cards.innervation: Anterior interosseous branch of median nerve (C7–C8)
cards.tip: Its tendon runs through the carpal tunnel; anterior interosseous nerve palsy weakens FPL and index FDP so the patient cannot make a round “OK” sign.

cards.name: Frontalis
cards.etymology: From Latin frons, frontis ‘forehead’. So it means ‘the forehead muscle’.
cards.origin: Epicranial aponeurosis (galea aponeurotica)
cards.insertion: Skin and fascia of eyebrows and forehead
cards.tip: Ask the patient to raise the eyebrows to test the temporal branch of CN VII (spared on the forehead in a central/stroke facial palsy, lost in Bell’s palsy).

cards.name: Geniohyoid
cards.etymology: From Greek geneion ‘chin’ + hyoeidēs ‘U-shaped’ (hyoid). So it means ‘the chin-to-hyoid muscle’.
cards.origin: Inferior mental spine (genial tubercle) of mandible
cards.insertion: Body of hyoid
actions: Depresses mandible when hyoid is fixed
cards.innervation: C1 fibres carried by the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
cards.tip: Sits just above the mylohyoid — supplied by C1 ‘hitch-hiking’ on CN XII.

cards.name: Iliococcygeus
cards.etymology: From Latin ilium ‘flank / hip bone’ + Greek kokkyx ‘cuckoo’ (coccyx, beak-shaped). So it means ‘the hip-bone-to-coccyx muscle’ — though it actually arises from the fascia over obturator internus and the ischial spine, not the ilium itself.
cards.origin: Posterior part of tendinous arch of levator ani (obturator fascia) and ischial spine
cards.insertion: Anococcygeal body and coccyx
cards.innervation: Nerve to levator ani (S3–S4) and pudendal nerve branches
cards.tip: The thin, flat posterolateral part of levator ani; overstretched in childbirth along with pubococcygeus.

cards.name: Iliocostalis cervicis (colli)
cards.etymology: From Latin ilium ‘hip bone’ + costa ‘rib’ + cervicis ‘of the neck’ (colli = of the neck, from collum). The neck segment of the ‘hip-to-rib’ column: it runs from ribs up to the neck.
cards.origin: Angles of ribs 3–6
cards.insertion: Posterior tubercles of transverse processes of C4–C6
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of cervical and upper thoracic spinal nerves
cards.tip: The uppermost iliocostalis — think of the column as overlapping relay segments climbing from pelvis to neck.

cards.name: Iliocostalis thoracis
cards.etymology: From Latin ilium ‘hip bone’ + costa ‘rib’ + thoracis ‘of the chest’. Despite the name it runs rib-to-rib — it is the thoracic segment of the ‘hip-to-rib’ column.
cards.origin: Angles of ribs 7–12 (medial to iliocostalis lumborum insertions)
cards.insertion: Angles of ribs 1–6 and transverse process of C7
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of thoracic spinal nerves
cards.tip: Helps maintain an upright thoracic posture; part of what keeps the upper back from rounding under load.

cards.name: Inferior gemellus
cards.etymology: From Latin inferior ‘lower’ + gemellus ‘little twin’. So it means ‘the lower little twin’ — the lower partner of the superior gemellus.
cards.origin: Upper part of the ischial tuberosity
cards.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter, blending with the obturator internus tendon
actions: Stabilises the femoral head in the acetabulum
cards.tip: Note the nerve split: superior gemellus goes with obturator internus, inferior gemellus with quadratus femoris.

cards.name: Innermost intercostals
cards.etymology: From English ‘innermost’ (Latin intimus, innermost) + inter ‘between’ + costa ‘rib’. So it means ‘the deepest muscles between the ribs’.
cards.origin: Internal surface of the rib above (lateral parts of intercostal spaces)
cards.insertion: Internal surface of the rib below
actions: Likely act with internal intercostals (rib depression in forced expiration)
cards.tip: Separated from the internal intercostals by the intercostal nerve, artery and vein — which run in the costal groove just under each rib.

cards.name: Lateral pterygoid
cards.etymology: From Greek pteryx ‘wing’ + eidos ‘form’ (pterygoid plates of the sphenoid) + Latin lateralis ‘of the side’. So it means ‘the outer wing-shaped-plate muscle’.
cards.origin: Superior head: infratemporal surface and crest of greater wing of sphenoid; inferior head: lateral surface of lateral pterygoid plate
cards.insertion: Pterygoid fovea on neck of mandibular condyle; superior head also into TMJ articular disc and capsule
actions: Mandible depression / mouth opening (inferior head pulls condyle forward)
Stabilises TMJ disc during closing (superior head)
cards.tip: Key TMJ muscle: it attaches to the articular disc, so its dysfunction is linked to disc displacement, clicking and jaw deviation on opening.

cards.name: Longissimus capitis
cards.etymology: From Latin longissimus ‘longest’ + capitis ‘of the head’. So it means ‘the longest muscle, head part’ — the only erector column that reaches the skull.
cards.origin: Transverse processes of T1–T4/T5 and articular processes of C4–C7
cards.insertion: Posterior margin of mastoid process of temporal bone
actions: Ipsilateral lateral flexion of head and neck
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of middle and lower cervical spinal nerves
cards.tip: Lies deep to splenius capitis and shares its mastoid attachment and same-side rotation.

cards.name: Longissimus cervicis (colli)
cards.etymology: From Latin longissimus ‘longest’ + cervicis ‘of the neck’ (colli, from collum, neck). So it means ‘the longest muscle, neck part’.
cards.origin: Transverse processes of T1–T5 (upper 4–6 thoracic vertebrae)
cards.insertion: Posterior tubercles of transverse processes of C2–C6
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of lower cervical and upper thoracic spinal nerves
cards.tip: Lies just medial to longissimus capitis; supports the neck in extension and posture.

cards.name: Longus capitis
cards.etymology: From Latin longus ‘long’ + capitis ‘of the head’ (caput). So it means ‘the long muscle of the head’ — a long prevertebral muscle running from the neck up to the skull.
cards.origin: Anterior tubercles of transverse processes of C3–C6
cards.insertion: Basilar part of occipital bone
cards.tip: Works with longus colli as a deep neck flexor; the ‘nod’ in a chin tuck comes from it.

cards.name: Longus colli
cards.etymology: From Latin longus ‘long’ + colli ‘of the neck’ (collum). So it means ‘the long muscle of the neck’ — it runs a long way down the front of the cervical and upper thoracic spine.
cards.origin: Bodies of T1–T3 and C5–C7; anterior tubercles of transverse processes of C3–C5
cards.insertion: Anterior tubercle of atlas; bodies of C2–C4; anterior tubercles of transverse processes of C5–C6
actions: Slight cervical rotation to the opposite side
cards.tip: A key deep neck flexor — weak in forward-head posture and after whiplash; train it with chin tucks / the craniocervical flexion test.

cards.name: Lumbricals (foot)
cards.etymology: From Latin lumbricus ‘earthworm’. So it means ‘the worm-like muscles’ — four small slender muscles between the flexor tendons.
cards.origin: Tendons of flexor digitorum longus
cards.insertion: Medial sides of the dorsal extensor expansions of toes 2–5
actions: Flexion of toes 2–5 at the MTP joints
Extension of toes 2–5 at the IP joints
cards.innervation: 1st: medial plantar nerve; 2nd–4th: lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3)
cards.tip: Help keep the toes flat on the ground during push-off; weakness contributes to claw/hammer toes.

cards.name: Lumbricals of the hand
cards.etymology: From Latin lumbricus ‘earthworm’. So it means ‘the earthworm-like muscles’ — four slender worm-shaped strands in the palm.
cards.origin: Tendons of flexor digitorum profundus (1st and 2nd: radial sides of tendons to digits 2–3; 3rd and 4th: adjacent sides of tendons to digits 3–5)
cards.insertion: Lateral (radial) sides of the extensor expansions of digits 2–5
cards.innervation: Lumbricals 1–2: median nerve (C8–T1); lumbricals 3–4: deep branch of ulnar nerve (C8–T1)
cards.tip: They create the “table-top” position (MCP flexed, IPs straight); unusually, they arise from a tendon rather than bone.

cards.name: Medial pterygoid
cards.etymology: From Greek pteryx ‘wing’ + eidos ‘form’ (the wing-like pterygoid plates of the sphenoid) + Latin medialis ‘toward the middle’. So it means ‘the inner wing-shaped-plate muscle’.
cards.origin: Deep head: medial surface of lateral pterygoid plate (and pyramidal process of palatine); superficial head: tuberosity of maxilla
cards.insertion: Medial surface of ramus near angle of mandible
cards.tip: Forms a ‘sling’ around the angle of the mandible with the masseter.

cards.name: Middle scalene
cards.etymology: From Greek skalēnos ‘uneven, unequal’ + Latin medius ‘middle’. So it means ‘the middle uneven muscle’ — the middle and largest of the three scalenes.
cards.origin: Posterior tubercles of transverse processes of C2–C7 (often also atlas)
cards.insertion: Superior surface of 1st rib, behind the groove for the subclavian artery
cards.tip: Forms the back wall of the interscalene triangle — part of the scalene-related thoracic outlet syndrome picture with the anterior scalene.

cards.name: Multifidus cervicis (colli)
cards.etymology: From Latin multus ‘many’ + -fidus ‘split’ + cervicis ‘of the neck’ (colli, from collum). So it means ‘split into many parts, of the neck’.
cards.origin: Articular processes of C4–C7
cards.insertion: Spinous processes of C2–C5 (2–4 segments above)
cards.innervation: Medial branches of dorsal rami of cervical spinal nerves
cards.tip: Part of the deep neck extensors that show altered activity and fatty infiltration after whiplash and in chronic neck pain.

cards.name: Multifidus thoracis
cards.etymology: From Latin multus ‘many’ + -fidus ‘split’ + thoracis ‘of the chest’. So it means ‘split into many parts, of the thoracic region’.
cards.origin: Transverse processes of thoracic vertebrae
cards.insertion: Spinous processes 2–4 segments above
cards.innervation: Medial branches of dorsal rami of thoracic spinal nerves
cards.tip: Thinner than the lumbar part; contributes to segmental control during thoracic rotation.

cards.name: Mylohyoid
cards.etymology: From Greek mylē ‘mill’ (referring to the molar or ‘grinding’ teeth) + hyoeidēs ‘U-shaped’ (hyoid). So it means ‘the molar-region-to-hyoid muscle’ — it arises from the mylohyoid line beneath the molars.
cards.origin: Mylohyoid line of mandible
cards.insertion: Median raphe and body of hyoid
actions: Elevates hyoid and floor of mouth (swallowing)
cards.tip: Forms the muscular floor of the mouth (‘oral diaphragm’).

cards.name: Obliquus capitis inferior
cards.etymology: From Latin obliquus ‘slanting’ + capitis ‘of the head’ + inferior ‘lower’. So it means ‘the lower slanting muscle of the head’ — even though, oddly, it never touches the skull.
cards.origin: Spinous process of axis (C2)
cards.insertion: Transverse process of atlas (C1)
actions: Head rotation to the same side (at the atlanto-axial joint)
cards.tip: The only ‘capitis’ muscle with no skull attachment — it turns C1 (and the head) on C2.

cards.name: Obliquus capitis superior
cards.etymology: From Latin obliquus ‘slanting’ + capitis ‘of the head’ + superior ‘upper’. So it means ‘the upper slanting muscle of the head’ — its fibres slant up and back from atlas to skull.
cards.origin: Transverse process of atlas (C1)
cards.insertion: Occipital bone between superior and inferior nuchal lines (lateral part)
cards.tip: Forms the upper-lateral side of the suboccipital triangle (vertebral artery and C1 run in its floor).

cards.name: Obturator externus
cards.etymology: From Latin obturare ‘to stop up, block’ + externus ‘outer’. So it means ‘the outer muscle of the blocked opening’ — it covers the outside of the obturator membrane.
cards.origin: External surface of the obturator membrane and surrounding bone of the obturator foramen
cards.insertion: Trochanteric fossa of the femur
actions: Stabilises the femoral head in the acetabulum
cards.tip: The only deep hip rotator supplied by the obturator nerve; it lies deep in the medial thigh, hidden by the adductors.

cards.name: Obturator internus
cards.etymology: From Latin obturare ‘to stop up, block’ + internus ‘inner’. So it means ‘the inner muscle of the blocked opening’ — it arises from the inside of the obturator membrane that closes the obturator foramen.
cards.origin: Inner (pelvic) surface of the obturator membrane and surrounding bone of the obturator foramen
cards.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter (after turning around the lesser sciatic notch)
actions: Stabilises the femoral head in the acetabulum
cards.tip: Its tendon makes a sharp turn through the lesser sciatic foramen, and its fascia also forms part of the pelvic side wall.

cards.name: Omohyoid
cards.etymology: From Greek ōmos ‘shoulder’ + hyoeidēs ‘U-shaped’ (hyoid). So it means ‘the shoulder-to-hyoid muscle’ — it runs from the scapula to the hyoid.
cards.origin: Inferior belly: superior border of scapula near suprascapular notch
cards.insertion: Superior belly: inferior border of body of hyoid (intermediate tendon tethered to clavicle by a fascial sling)
cards.tip: Two bellies with an intermediate tendon — a landmark dividing the anterior and posterior triangles of the neck.

cards.name: Opponens digiti minimi (hand)
cards.etymology: From Latin opponens ‘placing against’ + digiti minimi ‘of the smallest finger’. So it means ‘the muscle that sets the little finger against the thumb’.
cards.origin: Hook of hamate and flexor retinaculum
cards.insertion: Medial border of the 5th metacarpal
actions: Opposition of the little finger (draws the 5th metacarpal anteriorly and rotates it laterally)
Deepens the hollow of the palm (cupping)
cards.tip: Helps cup the palm for gripping round objects, working with opponens pollicis.

cards.name: Opponens pollicis
cards.etymology: From Latin opponens ‘placing against’ (ob ‘against’ + ponere ‘to place’) + pollicis ‘of the thumb’. So it means ‘the muscle that sets the thumb against the fingers’.
cards.origin: Flexor retinaculum and tubercle of trapezium
cards.insertion: Entire lateral border of the 1st metacarpal
actions: Thumb opposition (flexes and medially rotates the 1st metacarpal at the CMC joint)
cards.tip: Opposition is what makes the human grip — loss of it (median nerve injury) gives the flat “ape hand”.

cards.name: Palmar interossei
cards.etymology: From Latin palmaris ‘of the palm’ + inter ‘between’ + os/ossis ‘bone’. So it means ‘the muscles between the bones on the palm side’ (between the metacarpals).
cards.origin: Palmar surfaces of the 2nd, 4th and 5th metacarpals (unipennate; ulnar side of 2nd, radial sides of 4th and 5th)
cards.insertion: Bases of the proximal phalanges and extensor expansions of digits 2, 4 and 5
actions: Finger adduction (digits 2, 4, 5 toward the middle finger)
cards.tip: Mnemonic PAD — Palmar ADduct; test by gripping a card between straight fingers (card test for ulnar nerve).

cards.name: Palmaris longus
cards.etymology: From Latin palmaris ‘of the palm’ (palma) + longus ‘long’. So it means ‘the long muscle of the palm’ — a long tendon into the palmar aponeurosis.
cards.origin: Medial epicondyle of humerus (common flexor tendon)
cards.insertion: Distal half of the flexor retinaculum and the palmar aponeurosis
cards.tip: Absent in roughly 1 in 7 people; passes superficial to the carpal tunnel and is a favourite tendon graft (e.g. UCL “Tommy John” reconstruction).

cards.name: Pectoralis major — abdominal part
cards.etymology: From Latin pectoralis ‘of the chest’ (pectus, breast) + major ‘larger’. So it means ‘the larger chest muscle’ (vs pectoralis minor beneath it). ‘Abdominal’ is from Latin abdomen ‘belly’ — the slip arising from the abdominal wall aponeurosis.
cards.origin: Aponeurosis of external oblique muscle (anterior layer of rectus sheath)
cards.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of humerus (highest, deepest fibres of the twisted tendon)
actions: Shoulder extension from a flexed position
cards.tip: These fibres insert most superiorly and are most stretched at the bottom of a wide bench — the commonest site of pec tears.

cards.name: Plantar interossei
cards.etymology: From Latin plantaris ‘of the sole’ + inter ‘between’ + ossa ‘bones’. So it means ‘the muscles between the bones, on the sole side’ — three unipennate muscles.
cards.origin: Bases and medial sides of metatarsals 3–5
cards.insertion: Medial sides of the bases of the proximal phalanges of toes 3–5
cards.tip: ‘PAD’ — Plantar ADduct; three plantar vs four dorsal interossei.

cards.name: Plantaris
cards.etymology: From Latin planta ‘sole of the foot’ + -aris ‘relating to’. So it means ‘the muscle of the sole’ — in other animals it continues into the plantar fascia.
cards.origin: Lateral supracondylar line of the femur and oblique popliteal ligament
cards.insertion: Posterior calcaneus, medial to the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
cards.tip: Tiny belly with a very long thin tendon; absent in some people and harvested as a tendon graft.

cards.name: Popliteus
cards.etymology: From Latin poples ‘ham, back of the knee’. So it means ‘the muscle of the back of the knee’ — it lies in the floor of the popliteal fossa.
cards.origin: Lateral surface of the lateral femoral condyle and lateral meniscus
cards.insertion: Posterior surface of the tibia above the soleal line
actions: Unlocks the extended knee (femoral external rotation on fixed tibia / tibial internal rotation)
cards.tip: The ‘key that unlocks the knee’ — it reverses the screw-home mechanism at the start of knee flexion.

cards.name: Posterior scalene
cards.etymology: From Greek skalēnos ‘uneven, unequal’ + Latin posterior ‘behind’. So it means ‘the back uneven muscle’ — the smallest, most posterior scalene.
cards.origin: Posterior tubercles of transverse processes of C4–C6
cards.insertion: External surface of 2nd rib
cards.tip: The only scalene that reaches the 2nd rib — scalenes overwork as breathing muscles in apical/chest breathers.

cards.name: Pronator quadratus
cards.etymology: From Latin pronator ‘one that turns face-down’ + quadratus ‘squared, four-sided’. So it means ‘the square pronator’ across the distal forearm.
cards.origin: Distal quarter of the anterior surface of the ulna
cards.insertion: Distal quarter of the anterior surface of the radius
actions: Holds radius and ulna together at the distal radioulnar joint
cards.innervation: Anterior interosseous branch of median nerve (C7–C8)
cards.tip: The main pronator in all elbow positions — pronator teres joins in for fast or resisted pronation.

cards.name: Pronator teres
cards.etymology: From Latin pronator ‘one that turns face-down’ (pronus, bent forward) + teres ‘round, smooth’. So it means ‘the rounded pronator’.
cards.origin: Humeral (superficial) head: medial epicondyle (common flexor origin) and medial supracondylar ridge; ulnar (deep) head: medial side of the coronoid process of ulna
cards.insertion: Middle of the lateral surface of the radius (pronator tuberosity, point of maximum convexity)
cards.tip: The median nerve passes between its two heads — compression here (pronator syndrome) mimics carpal tunnel but includes palm numbness.

cards.name: Pubococcygeus
cards.etymology: From Latin pubis (os pubis, pubic bone) + Greek kokkyx ‘cuckoo’ (the coccyx, shaped like a cuckoo’s beak). So it means ‘the pubis-to-coccyx muscle’ — part of the levator ani sling.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of body of pubis and anterior part of tendinous arch of levator ani
cards.insertion: Anococcygeal body (ligament) and coccyx
cards.innervation: Nerve to levator ani (S3–S4) and pudendal nerve branches (S2–S4)
cards.tip: The ‘PC muscle’ targeted by Kegel exercises; it relaxes as the diaphragm descends and co-contracts with TrA in bracing.

cards.name: Puborectalis (pubo-analis)
cards.etymology: From Latin pubis ‘pubic bone’ + rectum ‘straight (gut)’ / anus ‘ring’. So it means ‘the pubis-to-rectum / anus muscle’ — a U-shaped sling from the pubis around the anorectal junction.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of body of pubis (either side of the symphysis)
cards.insertion: Loops behind the anorectal junction to join its partner; pubo-analis fibres blend into the anal canal wall between the sphincters
cards.innervation: Nerve to levator ani (S3–S4) and inferior rectal nerve (pudendal, S2–S4)
cards.tip: Paradoxical contraction of this sling during straining is a common cause of obstructed defecation — relaxation training helps.

cards.name: Pyramidalis
cards.etymology: From Latin pyramidalis ‘pyramid-shaped’ (Greek pyramis, pyramid). So it means ‘the pyramid-shaped muscle’ — a small triangle at the bottom of the rectus sheath, apex pointing up.
cards.origin: Pubic crest and pubic symphysis (anterior to rectus abdominis)
cards.insertion: Linea alba, about halfway to the umbilicus
cards.tip: Absent in roughly 10–20% of people; functionally minor.

cards.name: Quadratus femoris
cards.etymology: From Latin quadratus ‘squared, four-sided’ + femoris ‘of the thigh’. So it means ‘the square muscle of the thigh’ — a flat rectangular block below the gemelli.
cards.origin: Lateral border of the ischial tuberosity
cards.insertion: Quadrate tubercle on the intertrochanteric crest of the femur
actions: Stabilises the femoral head in the acetabulum
cards.tip: The lowest of the deep rotators seen from behind; can be pinched between ischium and femur (ischiofemoral impingement).

cards.name: Quadratus plantae
cards.etymology: From Latin quadratus ‘squared, four-sided’ + plantae ‘of the sole’. So it means ‘the square muscle of the sole’.
cards.origin: Medial and lateral surfaces of the plantar calcaneus (two heads)
cards.insertion: Lateral margin of the flexor digitorum longus tendon
actions: Straightens the oblique pull of FDL
cards.tip: Its alternative name ‘flexor accessorius’ says it all — a helper that redirects FDL’s pull in line with the toes.

cards.name: Rectus capitis posterior major
cards.etymology: From Latin rectus ‘straight’ + capitis ‘of the head’ + posterior ‘behind’ + major ‘larger’. So it means ‘the larger straight back muscle of the head’ — the bigger of the two straight suboccipital muscles.
cards.origin: Spinous process of axis (C2)
cards.insertion: Lateral part of inferior nuchal line of occipital bone
actions: Head rotation to the same side
cards.tip: Suboccipitals stay shortened in forward-head posture (chin poked, upper neck extended) and are a classic source of cervicogenic headache.

cards.name: Rectus capitis posterior minor
cards.etymology: From Latin rectus ‘straight’ + capitis ‘of the head’ + posterior ‘behind’ + minor ‘smaller’. So it means ‘the smaller straight back muscle of the head’ — the smaller, more medial straight suboccipital.
cards.origin: Posterior tubercle of atlas (C1)
cards.insertion: Medial part of inferior nuchal line of occipital bone
cards.tip: Has a connective-tissue ‘myodural bridge’ to the dura mater — linked to headaches in forward-head posture.

cards.name: Semispinalis cervicis (colli)
cards.etymology: From Latin semi ‘half’ + spinalis ‘of the spine’ + cervicis ‘of the neck’ (colli, from collum). Probably named because it spans the upper ‘half’ of the spine, transverse to spinous processes.
cards.origin: Transverse processes of T1–T6
cards.insertion: Spinous processes of C2–C5 (largest attachment on C2)
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of cervical spinal nerves
cards.tip: A major deep neck extensor that stabilises cervical lordosis; part of deep neck extensor training in neck pain rehab.

cards.name: Semispinalis thoracis
cards.etymology: From Latin semi ‘half’ + spinalis ‘of the spine’ + thoracis ‘of the chest’. Probably named because the semispinalis system covers roughly the upper half of the vertebral column; it runs transverse process to spinous process.
cards.origin: Transverse processes of T6–T10
cards.insertion: Spinous processes of C6–T4 (spanning 4–6 segments)
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of thoracic spinal nerves
cards.tip: The most superficial transversospinalis layer; longest fibres (4–6 segments) compared with multifidus (2–4) and rotatores (1–2).

cards.name: Serratus posterior inferior
cards.etymology: From Latin serratus ‘saw-toothed’ (serra, saw) + posterior ‘behind’ + inferior ‘lower’. So it means ‘the lower saw-toothed muscle at the back’, with tooth-like slips to the lowest ribs.
cards.origin: Spinous processes of T11–L2 and thoracolumbar fascia
cards.insertion: Inferior borders of ribs 9–12, near their angles
actions: Depresses and pulls back ribs 9–12 (possibly assists forced expiration or anchors ribs for diaphragm)
cards.innervation: Ventral rami of T9–T12 (lower intercostal and subcostal nerves)
cards.tip: Lies deep to the lats; its true respiratory function is uncertain.

cards.name: Serratus posterior superior
cards.etymology: From Latin serratus ‘saw-toothed’ (serra, saw) + posterior ‘behind’ + superior ‘upper’. So it means ‘the upper saw-toothed muscle at the back’ — its tooth-like slips attach to the ribs.
cards.origin: Ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes of C7–T3
cards.insertion: Superior borders of ribs 2–5, lateral to their angles
cards.tip: A thin respiratory muscle under the rhomboids; its role is debated and it is often blamed in vague upper-back pain.

cards.name: Spinalis thoracis
cards.etymology: From Latin spinalis ‘of the spine’ (spina, thorn / spinous process) + thoracis ‘of the chest’. So it means ‘the spinous-process muscle of the chest region’ — it runs spinous process to spinous process.
cards.origin: Spinous processes of T11–L2
cards.insertion: Spinous processes of T1–T8 (upper 4–8 thoracic)
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of thoracic spinal nerves
cards.tip: The smallest, most medial erector column — hugs the spinous processes.

cards.name: Splenius capitis
cards.etymology: From Greek splenion ‘bandage, patch’ + Latin capitis ‘of the head’. So it means ‘the bandage muscle of the head’ — it wraps like a strap over the deeper neck muscles up to the skull.
cards.origin: Lower half of ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes of C7–T3/T4
cards.insertion: Mastoid process of temporal bone and lateral third of superior nuchal line
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of middle cervical spinal nerves
cards.tip: Turns the head to the same side, working with the opposite SCM; a common culprit in tension-type neck pain and headaches.

cards.name: Splenius cervicis (colli)
cards.etymology: From Greek splenion ‘bandage, patch’ + Latin cervicis ‘of the neck’ (colli is the TA alternative, from collum, neck). So it means ‘the bandage muscle of the neck’ — the strap stops at the cervical vertebrae, not the skull.
cards.origin: Spinous processes of T3–T6
cards.insertion: Posterior tubercles of transverse processes of C1–C3
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of lower cervical spinal nerves
cards.tip: Lies just lateral and inferior to splenius capitis; same actions but on the cervical spine instead of the head.

cards.name: Sternohyoid
cards.etymology: From Greek sternon ‘chest, breastbone’ + hyoeidēs ‘U-shaped’ (hyoid). So it means ‘the sternum-to-hyoid muscle’.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of manubrium and medial end of clavicle
cards.insertion: Body of hyoid
cards.tip: Superficial ‘strap muscle’ of the infrahyoid group.

cards.name: Sternothyroid
cards.etymology: From Greek sternon ‘breastbone’ + thyreoeidēs ‘shield-shaped’ (thyreos ‘oblong shield’, the thyroid cartilage). So it means ‘the sternum-to-thyroid-cartilage muscle’.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of manubrium
cards.insertion: Oblique line of thyroid cartilage
cards.tip: Lies deep to sternohyoid; continues upward as thyrohyoid.

cards.name: Stylohyoid
cards.etymology: From Greek stylos ‘pillar, stake’ (the styloid process) + hyoeidēs ‘U-shaped’ (letter upsilon + eidos ‘form’, the hyoid bone). So it means ‘the styloid-to-hyoid muscle’.
cards.origin: Styloid process of temporal bone
cards.insertion: Body of hyoid (near greater horn); split around the digastric tendon
cards.tip: Its insertion splits to let the digastric’s intermediate tendon pass through.

cards.name: Subclavius
cards.etymology: From Latin sub ‘under’ + clavis/clavicula ‘(little) key, collarbone’. So it means ‘the muscle under the clavicle’.
cards.origin: Junction of the 1st rib and its costal cartilage
cards.insertion: Subclavian groove on the inferior surface of the middle third of the clavicle
cards.tip: Cushions the subclavian vessels and brachial plexus if the clavicle is fractured.

cards.name: Superior gemellus
cards.etymology: From Latin superior ‘upper’ + gemellus ‘little twin’ (diminutive of geminus ‘twin’). So it means ‘the upper little twin’ — paired with the inferior gemellus above and below the obturator internus tendon.
cards.origin: Ischial spine (outer surface)
cards.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter, blending with the obturator internus tendon
actions: Stabilises the femoral head in the acetabulum
cards.tip: One of the ‘deep six’ hip external rotators: piriformis, gemellus superior, obturator internus, gemellus inferior, quadratus femoris, obturator externus.

cards.name: Supinator
cards.etymology: From Latin supinare ‘to lay on the back, turn palm-up’ (supinus, lying face up). So it means ‘the muscle that turns the palm up’.
cards.origin: Lateral epicondyle of humerus, radial collateral and annular ligaments, supinator crest and fossa of ulna
cards.insertion: Lateral, posterior and anterior surfaces of the proximal third of the radius
actions: Forearm supination (especially with elbow extended or slow, unresisted)
cards.tip: The posterior interosseous nerve passes through it (arcade of Frohse) — radial tunnel syndrome mimics tennis elbow.

cards.name: Thyrohyoid
cards.etymology: From Greek thyreoeidēs ‘shield-shaped’ (thyroid cartilage) + hyoeidēs ‘U-shaped’ (hyoid). So it means ‘the thyroid-cartilage-to-hyoid muscle’.
cards.origin: Oblique line of thyroid cartilage
cards.insertion: Inferior border of body and greater horn of hyoid
actions: Elevates larynx when hyoid is fixed
cards.innervation: C1 fibres carried by the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
cards.tip: The one infrahyoid not supplied by the ansa cervicalis loop itself.

cards.name: Tibialis posterior
cards.etymology: From Latin tibia ‘shin bone’ + -alis ‘relating to’ + posterior ‘back’. So it means ‘the back shin-bone muscle’ — the deepest muscle at the back of the leg.
cards.origin: Interosseous membrane and adjacent posterior surfaces of the tibia and fibula
cards.insertion: Navicular tuberosity, plus cuneiforms, cuboid, sustentaculum tali and bases of metatarsals 2–4
cards.tip: Dysfunction causes adult flatfoot; first structure behind the medial malleolus — ‘Tom, Dick And Very Nervous Harry’.

cards.name: Transversus thoracis
cards.etymology: From Latin transversus ‘turned across’ + thoracis ‘of the chest’. So it means ‘the transverse muscle of the chest’ — it fans across the inside of the front chest wall.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of lower body of sternum and xiphoid process
cards.insertion: Internal surfaces of costal cartilages 2–6
cards.tip: Lies inside the chest wall, continuous below with transversus abdominis — think of it as TrA’s thoracic cousin.

cards.name: Zygomaticus major
cards.etymology: From Greek zygon ‘yoke’ (the zygomatic bone/arch joins face and skull like a yoke) + Latin major ‘larger’. So it means ‘the larger cheekbone muscle’.
cards.origin: Lateral surface of zygomatic bone (posterior part)
cards.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth
actions: Draws the angle of the mouth up and laterally (smiling)
cards.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), zygomatic and buccal branches
cards.tip: The main smiling muscle — ask the patient to smile to test lower CN VII.

cards.name: Distal phalanx of the 2nd toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Distal (from Latin distare ‘to stand apart’) means the one furthest away — the toe-tip bone.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the 2nd toe (DIP joint)
landmarks: Extensor digitorum longus/brevis via extensor expansion (dorsal base)
cards.tip: FDL inserts on the distal phalanges of toes 2–5, curling the toes to grip the ground.

cards.name: Distal phalanx of the 3rd toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Distal (from Latin distare ‘to stand apart’) means the one furthest away — the toe-tip bone.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the 3rd toe (DIP joint)
cards.tip: Mallet toe is fixed flexion at the DIP joint just proximal to this bone.

cards.name: Distal phalanx of the 4th toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Distal (from Latin distare ‘to stand apart’) means the one furthest away — the toe-tip bone.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the 4th toe (DIP joint)
cards.tip: A tiny tufted bone supporting the nail bed of the 4th toe.

cards.name: Distal phalanx of the 5th toe
aka: Distal phalanx of the little toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Distal (from Latin distare ‘to stand apart’) means the one furthest away — the toe-tip bone. The little toe is digitus minimus (hence ‘digiti minimi’).
articulations: Middle phalanx of the 5th toe (DIP joint)
landmarks: Often fused with the middle phalanx
cards.tip: The smallest phalanx in the foot; frequently fused with the middle phalanx.

cards.name: Distal phalanx of the big toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Distal (from Latin distare ‘to stand apart’) means the one furthest away — the toe-tip bone. The big toe is the hallux in Latin (hence ‘hallucis’ in muscle names); it has only two phalanges (no middle one).
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the big toe (IP joint)
cards.tip: FHL inserts here — the last tendon to push off the ground in gait.

cards.name: Distal phalanx of the index finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Distal (from Latin distare ‘to stand apart’) means the one furthest from the palm — the fingertip bone. Index is Latin ‘pointer’, from indicare ‘to point out’.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the index finger (DIP joint)
cards.tip: Mallet finger: the terminal extensor tendon pulls off its dorsal base and the DIP droops.

cards.name: Distal phalanx of the little finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Distal (from Latin distare ‘to stand apart’) means the one furthest from the palm — the fingertip bone. The little finger is digitus minimus in Latin (hence ‘digiti minimi’).
articulations: Middle phalanx of the little finger (DIP joint)
cards.tip: FDP to the ring and little fingers is supplied by the ulnar nerve — weak tip flexion here suggests ulnar nerve damage.

cards.name: Distal phalanx of the middle finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Distal (from Latin distare ‘to stand apart’) means the one furthest from the palm — the fingertip bone. The middle finger is digitus medius in Latin.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the middle finger (DIP joint)
cards.tip: Only FDP flexes the DIP joint — hold the middle phalanx still and bend the tip to test it.

cards.name: Distal phalanx of the ring finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Distal (from Latin distare ‘to stand apart’) means the one furthest from the palm — the fingertip bone. The ring finger is digitus anularis in Latin (anulus ‘ring’).
articulations: Middle phalanx of the ring finger (DIP joint)
cards.tip: Jersey finger — FDP avulsion from its base when grabbing a shirt — most often involves the ring finger.

cards.name: Distal phalanx of the thumb
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Distal (from Latin distare ‘to stand apart’) means the one furthest from the palm — the fingertip bone. The thumb is pollex in Latin (hence ‘pollicis’ in muscle names). The thumb has only two phalanges (no middle one).
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the thumb (IP joint)
cards.tip: FPL is the only muscle that flexes the thumb IP joint — bending the thumb tip tests it (anterior interosseous nerve).

cards.name: Incus
cards.etymology: Latin incus ‘anvil’. So it means ‘the anvil’ — the hammer (malleus) appears to strike it.
cards.tip: The middle of the three ossicles, passing vibration from malleus to stapes.

cards.name: Inferior nasal concha
cards.etymology: From Latin concha ‘shell’ (Greek konchē ‘mussel, shell’). So it means ‘the lower shell of the nose’ — a curled, shell-like scroll of bone on the lateral nasal wall.
landmarks: Overhangs the inferior meatus (opening of the nasolacrimal duct)
cards.tip: Unlike the superior and middle conchae (parts of the ethmoid) it is a separate bone.

cards.name: Lacrimal bone
cards.etymology: From Latin lacrima ‘tear’. So it means ‘the tear bone’ — it holds the lacrimal (tear) sac in the inner wall of the orbit.
cards.tip: The smallest and most fragile facial bone, in the medial wall of the orbit.

cards.name: Malleus
cards.etymology: Latin malleus ‘hammer, mallet’. So it means ‘the hammer’ — its handle and head look like a small hammer.
cards.tip: Tensor tympani inserts on its handle to damp loud sounds.

cards.name: Middle phalanx of the 2nd toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Middle means the second of the three.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the 2nd toe (PIP joint)
Distal phalanx of the 2nd toe (DIP joint)
landmarks: Flexor digitorum brevis (both sides of the shaft)
cards.tip: In a hammer toe the PIP joint between this bone and the proximal phalanx is fixed in flexion.

cards.name: Middle phalanx of the 3rd toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Middle means the second of the three.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the 3rd toe (PIP joint)
Distal phalanx of the 3rd toe (DIP joint)
landmarks: Flexor digitorum brevis (both sides of the shaft)
cards.tip: Flexor digitorum brevis (‘short toe flexor’) inserts on the middle phalanges of toes 2–5 and flexes the PIP joints.

cards.name: Middle phalanx of the 4th toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Middle means the second of the three.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the 4th toe (PIP joint)
Distal phalanx of the 4th toe (DIP joint)
landmarks: Flexor digitorum brevis (both sides of the shaft)
cards.tip: Middle phalanges of the lesser toes are short, almost cube-like bones.

cards.name: Middle phalanx of the 5th toe
aka: Middle phalanx of the little toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Middle means the second of the three. The little toe is digitus minimus (hence ‘digiti minimi’).
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the 5th toe (PIP joint)
Distal phalanx of the 5th toe (DIP joint)
landmarks: Flexor digitorum brevis slip (often small or absent)
Frequently fused with the distal phalanx (symphalangism)
cards.tip: Often fused with the distal phalanx, so many little toes appear to have only two phalanges.

cards.name: Middle phalanx of the index finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Middle means the second of the three. Index is Latin ‘pointer’, from indicare ‘to point out’.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the index finger (PIP joint)
Distal phalanx of the index finger (DIP joint)
landmarks: Base with two concave facets and a median ridge
Flexor digitorum superficialis splits to insert on both sides of the shaft
Central slip of the extensor expansion (dorsal base)
cards.tip: Test index FDS by holding the other fingers straight and asking for PIP flexion.

cards.name: Middle phalanx of the little finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Middle means the second of the three. The little finger is digitus minimus in Latin (hence ‘digiti minimi’).
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the little finger (PIP joint)
Distal phalanx of the little finger (DIP joint)
landmarks: Base with two concave facets and a median ridge
Shortest middle phalanx of the hand
FDS insertion (tendon sometimes small or absent)
Central slip of extensor expansion (dorsal base)
cards.tip: Little-finger FDS is weak or absent in some people, so PIP flexion may rely on FDP.

cards.name: Middle phalanx of the middle finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Middle means the second of the three. The middle finger is digitus medius in Latin.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the middle finger (PIP joint)
Distal phalanx of the middle finger (DIP joint)
landmarks: Base with two concave facets and a median ridge
FDS insertion on both sides of the shaft
Central slip of extensor expansion (dorsal base)
cards.tip: The middle finger is the longest digit, and its middle phalanx is usually the longest one in the hand.

cards.name: Middle phalanx of the ring finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Middle means the second of the three. The ring finger is digitus anularis in Latin (anulus ‘ring’).
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the ring finger (PIP joint)
Distal phalanx of the ring finger (DIP joint)
landmarks: Base with two concave facets and a median ridge
FDS insertion on both sides of the shaft
Central slip of extensor expansion (dorsal base)
cards.tip: Rupture of the central slip at its base gives a boutonnière deformity (PIP flexed, DIP hyperextended).

cards.name: Palatine bone
cards.etymology: From Latin palatum ‘palate, roof of the mouth’. So it means ‘the palate bone’ — its horizontal plate forms the back of the hard palate.
cards.tip: Forms the posterior third of the hard palate; the soft palate hangs from its back edge.

cards.name: Proximal phalanx of the 2nd toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Proximal (Latin proximus ‘nearest’) means the one nearest the sole.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the 2nd toe (PIP joint)
cards.tip: The 2nd toe is the foot’s axis, so only dorsal interossei attach to it; hammer toe most often involves this toe.

cards.name: Proximal phalanx of the 3rd toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Proximal (Latin proximus ‘nearest’) means the one nearest the sole.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the 3rd toe (PIP joint)
cards.tip: Plantar interossei adduct toes 3–5 toward the 2nd toe; dorsal interossei abduct away from it.

cards.name: Proximal phalanx of the 4th toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Proximal (Latin proximus ‘nearest’) means the one nearest the sole.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the 4th toe (PIP joint)
cards.tip: Lesser-toe proximal phalanges are long and slender compared with the stubby middle and distal ones.

cards.name: Proximal phalanx of the 5th toe
aka: Proximal phalanx of the little toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Proximal (Latin proximus ‘nearest’) means the one nearest the sole. The little toe is digitus minimus (hence ‘digiti minimi’).
articulations: Middle phalanx of the 5th toe (PIP joint)
landmarks: Abductor digiti minimi and flexor digiti minimi brevis (lateral base)
cards.tip: A stubbed little toe most often fractures this phalanx.

cards.name: Proximal phalanx of the big toe
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the toe bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Proximal (Latin proximus ‘nearest’) means the one nearest the sole. The big toe is the hallux in Latin (hence ‘hallucis’ in muscle names); it has only two phalanges (no middle one).
articulations: Distal phalanx of the big toe (IP joint)
landmarks: Flexor hallucis brevis (both sides of base, via the sesamoids)
cards.tip: Hallux valgus drifts it laterally on the 1st metatarsal head; ‘turf toe’ is a plantar-plate sprain at its base.

cards.name: Proximal phalanx of the index finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Proximal (Latin proximus ‘nearest’) means the one nearest the palm. Index is Latin ‘pointer’, from indicare ‘to point out’.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the index finger (PIP joint)
landmarks: 1st dorsal interosseous (radial side of base/extensor expansion)
cards.tip: The 1st dorsal interosseous abducts the index on this bone — the muscle bulk in the first web space.

cards.name: Proximal phalanx of the little finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Proximal (Latin proximus ‘nearest’) means the one nearest the palm. The little finger is digitus minimus in Latin (hence ‘digiti minimi’).
articulations: Middle phalanx of the little finger (PIP joint)
landmarks: Abductor digiti minimi and flexor digiti minimi brevis (ulnar side of base)
cards.tip: The hypothenar muscles insert on its base, so it moves with the little-finger side of the palm.

cards.name: Proximal phalanx of the middle finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Proximal (Latin proximus ‘nearest’) means the one nearest the palm. The middle finger is digitus medius in Latin.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the middle finger (PIP joint)
cards.tip: The middle finger is the axis for finger abduction/adduction, so only dorsal interossei attach to it — one on each side.

cards.name: Proximal phalanx of the ring finger
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Proximal (Latin proximus ‘nearest’) means the one nearest the palm. The ring finger is digitus anularis in Latin (anulus ‘ring’).
articulations: Middle phalanx of the ring finger (PIP joint)
cards.tip: Palmar interossei adduct toward the middle finger, dorsal ones abduct away — here they pull on opposite sides of the base.

cards.name: Proximal phalanx of the thumb
cards.etymology: From Greek phalanx ‘a line of soldiers in battle formation’ (plural phalanges) — the finger bones are lined up in rows like ranks of soldiers. Proximal (Latin proximus ‘nearest’) means the one nearest the palm. The thumb is pollex in Latin (hence ‘pollicis’ in muscle names). The thumb has only two phalanges (no middle one).
articulations: Distal phalanx of the thumb (IP joint)
landmarks: Abductor pollicis brevis and flexor pollicis brevis (radial base, via the radial sesamoid)
Adductor pollicis (ulnar base, via the ulnar sesamoid)
cards.tip: Skier’s/gamekeeper’s thumb is a tear of the ulnar collateral ligament at the MCP joint on its base.

cards.name: Sesamoid bones of the foot (hallux sesamoids)
cards.etymology: From Greek sēsamon ‘sesame seed’ + -oeidēs ‘like’. So it means ‘shaped like a sesame seed’ — small, oval bones embedded in tendons.
articulations: Plantar surface of the 1st metatarsal head (grooves)
landmarks: Within the two tendons of flexor hallucis brevis
Attachments of abductor hallucis (medial) and adductor hallucis (lateral)
cards.tip: They take load under the big-toe ball and protect the FHL tendon; sesamoiditis is common in runners and dancers.

cards.name: Stapes
cards.etymology: Medieval Latin stapes ‘stirrup’. So it means ‘the stirrup’ — two crura and a footplate look exactly like a stirrup.
articulations: Oval window (footplate held by annular ligament)
cards.tip: The smallest bone in the body; stapedius (the smallest muscle) attaches to its neck.

cards.name: Vomer
cards.etymology: Latin vomer ‘ploughshare’. So it means ‘the ploughshare bone’ — a thin blade shaped like a plough blade.
landmarks: Posteroinferior part of the nasal septum
cards.tip: With the ethmoid’s perpendicular plate it forms the bony nasal septum — a deviated septum often involves it.

cards.name: Adductor minimus
cards.etymology: From Latin adducere ‘to lead towards’ + minimus ‘smallest’. So it means ‘the smallest muscle that draws the leg in’ — a name for the uppermost slip of adductor magnus.
cards.origin: Inferior pubic ramus (upper, most anterior fibres of adductor magnus)
cards.insertion: Gluteal tuberosity and upper linea aspera of the femur
cards.tip: Not a separate muscle in most texts — it is the upper, horizontal part of adductor magnus, often partly separated from it.

cards.name: Buccinator
cards.etymology: From Latin buccinator ‘trumpeter’, from buccina ‘trumpet’ (related to bucca ‘cheek’). So it means ‘the trumpeter’s muscle’ — it compresses the cheek to blow air out.
cards.origin: Alveolar processes of maxilla and mandible opposite the molars, and pterygomandibular raphe
cards.insertion: Angle of the mouth, blending into orbicularis oris
actions: Compresses the cheek against the teeth (keeps food between molars)
cards.tip: Motor by CN VII — don’t confuse with the buccal nerve of CN V3, which is only sensory to the cheek.

cards.name: Corrugator supercilii
cards.etymology: From Latin corrugare ‘to wrinkle’ (com- + ruga ‘wrinkle’) + supercilii ‘of the eyebrow’ (supercilium). So it means ‘the eyebrow wrinkler’.
cards.origin: Medial end of superciliary arch of frontal bone
cards.insertion: Skin above the middle of the eyebrow
actions: Produces vertical frown lines between the brows
cards.tip: The ‘worried frown’ muscle — a common target of cosmetic botulinum toxin.

cards.name: Cricothyroid
cards.etymology: From Greek krikos ‘ring’ (cricoid cartilage) + thyreoeidēs ‘shield-shaped’ (thyroid cartilage). So it means ‘the ring-to-shield muscle’ — between the cricoid and thyroid cartilages.
cards.origin: Anterolateral surface of cricoid arch
cards.insertion: Straight part: inferior margin of thyroid lamina; oblique part: inferior horn of thyroid cartilage
actions: Tilts thyroid cartilage forward on cricoid
Lengthens and tenses the vocal folds (raises pitch)
cards.innervation: External laryngeal nerve (branch of superior laryngeal nerve, CN X)
cards.tip: The only intrinsic laryngeal muscle NOT supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve; injury (e.g. thyroid surgery) loses high notes.

cards.name: Depressor anguli oris
cards.etymology: From Latin depressor ‘one that presses down’ + anguli ‘of the corner’ + oris ‘of the mouth’. So it means ‘the puller-down of the corner of the mouth’.
cards.origin: Oblique line of mandible, below the canine and premolars
cards.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth
actions: Depresses the angle of the mouth (frowning, sadness)
cards.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), marginal mandibular branch
cards.tip: Triangular in shape — the ‘sad face’ muscle.

cards.name: Depressor labii inferioris
cards.etymology: From Latin depressor ‘one that presses down’ + labii ‘of the lip’ + inferioris ‘lower’. So it means ‘the puller-down of the lower lip’.
cards.origin: Oblique line of mandible, between the symphysis and mental foramen (deep to depressor anguli oris)
cards.insertion: Skin and mucosa of the lower lip
actions: Depresses the lower lip and draws it laterally
Everts the lower lip (pouting, showing lower teeth)
cards.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), marginal mandibular branch
cards.tip: Weakness gives an asymmetric lower lip when showing the teeth — a sign of marginal mandibular nerve injury.

cards.name: Depressor septi nasi
cards.etymology: From Latin depressor ‘one that presses down’ + septi ‘of the partition’ (septum ‘fence, partition’) + nasi ‘of the nose’. So it means ‘the puller-down of the nasal septum’.
cards.origin: Incisive fossa of maxilla
cards.insertion: Mobile part of nasal septum and ala
cards.tip: Its pull drops the nasal tip when smiling.

cards.name: Genioglossus
cards.etymology: From Greek geneion ‘chin’ + glōssa ‘tongue’. So it means ‘the chin-to-tongue muscle’.
cards.origin: Superior mental spine (genial tubercle) of mandible
cards.insertion: Dorsum of tongue and body of hyoid
actions: Depresses the centre of the tongue
Deviates tongue to the opposite side (unilateral)
cards.tip: With a CN XII lesion the protruded tongue deviates TOWARD the weak side; genioglossus also keeps the airway open in sleep.

cards.name: Hyoglossus
cards.etymology: From Greek hyoeidēs ‘U-shaped’ (hyoid) + glōssa ‘tongue’. So it means ‘the hyoid-to-tongue muscle’.
cards.origin: Body and greater horn of hyoid
cards.insertion: Side and inferior surface of the tongue
cards.tip: Landmark in the floor of mouth: lingual nerve and CN XII lie on it, lingual artery runs deep to it.

cards.name: Inferior oblique
cards.etymology: From Latin inferior ‘lower’ + obliquus ‘slanting’. So it means ‘the lower slanting muscle’ of the eye.
cards.origin: Orbital surface of maxilla, anteromedial floor of orbit (lateral to nasolacrimal groove)
cards.insertion: Sclera, posteroinferolateral quadrant (deep to lateral rectus)
cards.tip: Test by looking in (adduct) then up. The only extra-ocular muscle not arising at the back of the orbit.

cards.name: Inferior pharyngeal constrictor
cards.etymology: From Latin inferior ‘lower’ + Greek pharynx ‘throat’ + Latin constrictor ‘one that draws tight’. So it means ‘the lower throat squeezer’.
cards.origin: Oblique line of thyroid cartilage (thyropharyngeus) and side of cricoid cartilage (cricopharyngeus)
cards.insertion: Median pharyngeal raphe; cricopharyngeus encircles the pharyngo-oesophageal junction
actions: Cricopharyngeus acts as the upper oesophageal sphincter
cards.innervation: Vagus nerve (CN X) via pharyngeal plexus, plus external and recurrent laryngeal branches
cards.tip: A weak spot between its two parts (Killian’s dehiscence) is where a Zenker’s diverticulum forms.

cards.name: Inferior rectus
cards.etymology: From Latin inferior ‘lower’ + rectus ‘straight’. So it means ‘the lower straight muscle’ of the eye.
cards.origin: Common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn)
cards.insertion: Inferior sclera, anterior to the equator of the eyeball
cards.tip: Test in the H-pattern: look out (abduct) then down. Can be entrapped in an orbital floor ‘blow-out’ fracture.

cards.name: Interspinales cervicis (colli)
cards.etymology: From Latin inter ‘between’ + spina ‘spinous process’ + cervicis ‘of the neck’ (colli, from collum). So it means ‘the muscles between the neck’s spinous processes’.
cards.origin: Spinous processes of C3–T1
cards.insertion: Spinous process of the vertebra above (from C2 down), paired either side of the bifid tips
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of cervical spinal nerves
cards.tip: Best developed in the neck, where bifid spinous processes give each side its own little muscle.

cards.name: Interspinales lumborum
cards.etymology: From Latin inter ‘between’ + spina ‘thorn / spinous process’ + lumborum ‘of the loins’. So it means ‘the muscles between the spinous processes of the low back’.
cards.origin: Superior surface of lumbar spinous processes
cards.insertion: Inferior surface of the spinous process immediately above
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of lumbar spinal nerves
cards.tip: Four or so short pairs either side of the interspinous ligament; mainly sensory/stabilising.
