cards.name: Interspinales thoracis
cards.etymology: From Latin inter ‘between’ + spina ‘spinous process’ + thoracis ‘of the chest’. So it means ‘the muscles between the thoracic spinous processes’.
cards.origin: Spinous processes of thoracic vertebrae (usually only at the top, T1–T2, and bottom, T11–T12)
cards.insertion: Spinous process of the adjacent vertebra above
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of thoracic spinal nerves
cards.tip: Often absent through the mid-thoracic spine, where the overlapping spinous processes leave little room.

cards.name: Lateral crico-arytenoid
cards.etymology: From Greek krikos ‘ring’ (cricoid) + arytaina ‘ladle’ + eidos ‘form’ (arytenoid) + Latin lateralis ‘of the side’. So it means ‘the side ring-to-ladle muscle’.
cards.origin: Arch of cricoid cartilage
cards.insertion: Muscular process of arytenoid cartilage
actions: Adducts the vocal folds (closes the interligamentous rima glottidis)
cards.tip: Direct antagonist of the posterior crico-arytenoid.

cards.name: Lateral intertransversarii lumborum (dorsal part)
cards.etymology: From Latin inter ‘between’ + transversus ‘turned across’ (transverse process) + lateralis ‘side’ + dorsalis ‘back’ + lumborum ‘of the loins’. So it means ‘the back slips of the side muscles between lumbar transverse processes’.
cards.origin: Accessory process of a lumbar vertebra
cards.insertion: Transverse process of the vertebra above
cards.innervation: Ventral rami of lumbar spinal nerves
cards.tip: Tiny segmental muscles — more sensors and stabilisers than movers.

cards.name: Lateral intertransversarii lumborum (ventral part)
cards.etymology: From Latin inter ‘between’ + transversus ‘turned across’ (transverse process) + lateralis ‘side’ + ventralis ‘belly / front’ + lumborum ‘of the loins’. So it means ‘the front slips of the side muscles between lumbar transverse processes’.
cards.origin: Transverse process of a lumbar vertebra
cards.insertion: Transverse process of the vertebra above
cards.innervation: Ventral rami of lumbar spinal nerves
cards.tip: Embryologically related to the intercostals, which is why they are supplied by ventral rami.

cards.name: Lateral rectus
cards.etymology: From Latin lateralis ‘of the side’ + rectus ‘straight’. So it means ‘the outer straight muscle’ of the eye.
cards.origin: Common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn)
cards.insertion: Lateral sclera, anterior to the equator of the eyeball
cards.tip: ‘LR6’: abducens abducts — a CN VI palsy means the eye cannot look outward (horizontal double vision).

cards.name: Levator anguli oris
cards.etymology: From Latin levator ‘lifter’ + anguli ‘of the corner’ (angulus) + oris ‘of the mouth’ (os). So it means ‘the lifter of the corner of the mouth’.
cards.origin: Canine fossa of maxilla, below the infra-orbital foramen
cards.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth
actions: Elevates the angle of the mouth
cards.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), zygomatic and buccal branches
cards.tip: Deep to levator labii superioris — helps produce a closed-lip smile.

cards.name: Levator labii superioris
cards.etymology: From Latin levator ‘lifter’ + labii ‘of the lip’ (labium) + superioris ‘upper’. So it means ‘the lifter of the upper lip’.
cards.origin: Infra-orbital margin of maxilla, above the infra-orbital foramen
cards.insertion: Skin and muscle of the upper lip
cards.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), zygomatic and buccal branches
cards.tip: Lies between levator labii superioris alaeque nasi (medial) and zygomaticus minor (lateral).

cards.name: Levator labii superioris alaeque nasi
cards.etymology: From Latin levator ‘lifter’ + labii superioris ‘of the upper lip’ + alaeque nasi ‘and of the wing of the nose’ (ala ‘wing’, -que ‘and’, nasus ‘nose’). So it means ‘the lifter of the upper lip and the wing of the nose’.
cards.origin: Frontal process of maxilla
cards.insertion: Alar cartilage of the nose and skin of upper lip
cards.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), zygomatic and buccal branches
cards.tip: Famous for having the longest muscle name — the ‘Elvis sneer’ muscle.

cards.name: Levator palpebrae superioris
cards.etymology: From Latin levator ‘lifter’ + palpebrae ‘of the eyelid’ (palpebra) + superioris ‘upper’. So it means ‘the lifter of the upper eyelid’.
cards.origin: Lesser wing of sphenoid, above and in front of the optic canal
cards.insertion: Skin and tarsal plate of the upper eyelid (via its aponeurosis)
cards.innervation: Oculomotor nerve (CN III), superior division; smooth superior tarsal part by sympathetics
cards.tip: Ptosis = CN III palsy (complete droop) or Horner’s syndrome (mild droop from the sympathetic superior tarsal muscle).

cards.name: Levatores costarum breves
cards.etymology: From Latin levatores ‘lifters’ (levare, to raise) + costarum ‘of the ribs’ (costa, rib) + breves ‘short’. So it means ‘the short rib-lifters’ — each spans just one segment.
cards.origin: Tips of transverse processes of C7–T11
cards.insertion: Outer surface of the rib immediately below, between tubercle and angle
actions: Ipsilateral lateral flexion and contralateral rotation of thoracic spine (minor)
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of C8–T11 spinal nerves
cards.tip: Small fan-shaped muscles; mostly of interest for respiration and segmental thoracic mobility.

cards.name: Levatores costarum longi
cards.etymology: From Latin levatores ‘lifters’ + costarum ‘of the ribs’ + longi ‘long’. So it means ‘the long rib-lifters’ — they skip one rib.
cards.origin: Transverse processes of lower thoracic vertebrae (approximately T7–T10)
cards.insertion: Rib two levels below, between tubercle and angle (skipping one rib)
actions: Ipsilateral lateral flexion and contralateral rotation of thoracic spine (minor)
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of thoracic spinal nerves
cards.tip: Found only in the lower thorax; the ‘longi’ simply cross two segments instead of one.

cards.name: Medial rectus
cards.etymology: From Latin medialis ‘toward the middle’ + rectus ‘straight’. So it means ‘the inner straight muscle’ of the eye.
cards.origin: Common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn)
cards.insertion: Medial sclera, anterior to the equator of the eyeball
cards.tip: Remember ‘LR6 SO4, the rest 3’ — medial rectus is CN III; with a CN III palsy the eye rests ‘down and out’.

cards.name: Mentalis
cards.etymology: From Latin mentum ‘chin’. So it means ‘the chin muscle’.
cards.origin: Incisive fossa of mandible
cards.insertion: Skin of the chin
actions: Elevates and protrudes the lower lip (pouting, drinking)
Wrinkles the skin of the chin
cards.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), marginal mandibular branch
cards.tip: The ‘dimpled/golf-ball chin’ muscle when you push your lower lip up.

cards.name: Middle pharyngeal constrictor
cards.etymology: From Latin medius ‘middle’ + Greek pharynx ‘throat’ + Latin constrictor ‘one that draws tight’. So it means ‘the middle throat squeezer’.
cards.origin: Stylohyoid ligament and greater and lesser horns of hyoid
cards.insertion: Median pharyngeal raphe
cards.innervation: Vagus nerve (CN X) via pharyngeal plexus
cards.tip: Fan-shaped from the hyoid — the constrictors overlap like stacked cups, inferior outside middle outside superior.

cards.name: Nasalis
cards.etymology: From Latin nasus ‘nose’. So it means ‘the nose muscle’.
cards.origin: Maxilla lateral to the nose, above the incisor and canine teeth
cards.insertion: Transverse part: aponeurosis over nasal bridge; alar part: alar cartilage
cards.tip: Flaring nostrils (alar part) is a sign of increased work of breathing.

cards.name: Oblique arytenoid (aryepiglottic part)
cards.etymology: From Latin obliquus ‘slanting’ + Greek arytaina ‘ladle’ + eidos ‘form’ (arytenoid); aryepiglottic adds epi ‘upon’ + glōttis ‘mouth of the windpipe’. So it means ‘the slanting arytenoid muscle continuing to the epiglottis’.
cards.origin: Muscular process of one arytenoid cartilage
cards.insertion: Apex of the opposite arytenoid, continuing in the aryepiglottic fold to the lateral margin of the epiglottis
actions: Closes the laryngeal inlet (sphincter during swallowing)
Draws the arytenoids together (adducts vocal folds)
cards.tip: The two oblique arytenoids cross in an X behind the transverse arytenoid.

cards.name: Occipitalis
cards.etymology: From Latin occiput ‘back of the head’ (ob ‘against, behind’ + caput ‘head’). So it means ‘the back-of-the-head muscle’.
cards.origin: Lateral two-thirds of superior nuchal line and mastoid process
cards.insertion: Epicranial aponeurosis
cards.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), posterior auricular branch
cards.tip: Paired with frontalis through the galea as one ‘occipitofrontalis’ unit.

cards.name: Opponens digiti minimi (foot)
aka: Opponens digiti minimi muscle of foot
cards.etymology: From Latin opponens ‘placing against’ + digiti ‘of the digit’ + minimi ‘smallest’. So it means ‘the opposer of the little toe’ — named after its hand counterpart, though the toe can’t truly oppose.
cards.origin: Long plantar ligament and sheath of the fibularis longus tendon
cards.insertion: Lateral border of the 5th metatarsal
actions: Draws the 5th metatarsal medially and plantarward (deepens the lateral sole)
cards.tip: Inconstant — many texts treat it as a deep slip of flexor digiti minimi brevis rather than a separate muscle.

cards.name: Orbicularis oculi
cards.etymology: From Latin orbiculus ‘small disc, little circle’ + oculi ‘of the eye’ (oculus). So it means ‘the little circular muscle of the eye’ — a sphincter ring around the eye.
cards.origin: Nasal part of frontal bone, frontal process of maxilla, medial palpebral ligament (and lacrimal bone, lacrimal part)
cards.insertion: Skin around the orbit; palpebral part to lateral palpebral raphe
actions: Forced, tight eyelid closure / squinting (orbital part)
cards.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), temporal and zygomatic branches
cards.tip: Inability to close the eye tightly is a hallmark of Bell’s palsy (CN VII).

cards.name: Orbicularis oris
cards.etymology: From Latin orbiculus ‘little circle’ + oris ‘of the mouth’ (os). So it means ‘the little circular muscle of the mouth’ — a sphincter around the lips.
cards.origin: Maxilla and mandible near the midline, and fibres from surrounding facial muscles (esp. buccinator)
cards.insertion: Skin and mucous membrane of the lips
actions: Protrudes and purses the lips (whistling, kissing)
cards.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), buccal and marginal mandibular branches
cards.tip: Test CN VII by asking the patient to puff the cheeks with lips sealed.

cards.name: Palatopharyngeus
cards.etymology: From Latin palatum ‘palate, roof of the mouth’ + Greek pharynx ‘throat’. So it means ‘the palate-to-throat muscle’.
cards.origin: Hard palate and palatine aponeurosis
cards.insertion: Lateral pharyngeal wall and posterior border of thyroid cartilage
actions: Elevates pharynx and larynx during swallowing
Draws palatopharyngeal arches together, helping close off the nasopharynx
cards.innervation: Vagus nerve (CN X) via pharyngeal plexus
cards.tip: Forms the palatopharyngeal arch (posterior pillar) behind the palatine tonsil.

cards.name: Posterior crico-arytenoid
cards.etymology: From Greek krikos ‘ring’ (cricoid) + arytaina ‘ladle, pitcher’ + eidos ‘form’ (arytenoid, ladle-shaped) + Latin posterior ‘behind’. So it means ‘the back ring-to-ladle muscle’.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of cricoid lamina
cards.insertion: Muscular process of arytenoid cartilage
actions: Abducts the vocal folds (opens the rima glottidis)
cards.tip: The ONLY abductor of the vocal folds — bilateral loss threatens the airway (‘safety muscle of the larynx’).

cards.name: Procerus
cards.etymology: From Latin procerus ‘long, stretched out, tall’. So it means ‘the long (slender) muscle’ — probably for its elongated shape running up the bridge of the nose.
cards.origin: Fascia over nasal bone and upper lateral nasal cartilage
cards.insertion: Skin of lower forehead between the eyebrows
actions: Makes transverse wrinkles over the bridge of the nose
cards.tip: Creates the horizontal ‘bunny line’ at the nose bridge when frowning or squinting into sun.

cards.name: Rectus capitis anterior
cards.etymology: From Latin rectus ‘straight’ + capitis ‘of the head’ + anterior ‘front’. So it means ‘the straight front muscle of the head’ — a short, straight muscle in front of the atlanto-occipital joint.
cards.origin: Anterior surface of lateral mass of atlas (C1)
cards.insertion: Basilar part of occipital bone, in front of the occipital condyle
actions: Head flexion at the atlanto-occipital joint
cards.tip: Tiny deep craniocervical flexor — the anterior counterpart of the suboccipitals.

cards.name: Rectus capitis lateralis
cards.etymology: From Latin rectus ‘straight’ + capitis ‘of the head’ + lateralis ‘of the side’. So it means ‘the straight side muscle of the head’ — a short vertical muscle on the side of the atlanto-occipital joint.
cards.origin: Superior surface of transverse process of atlas (C1)
cards.insertion: Jugular process of occipital bone
cards.tip: Considered the upper-cervical equivalent of a posterior intertransverse muscle.

cards.name: Risorius
cards.etymology: From Latin risus ‘laughter’ (ridere ‘to laugh’). So it means ‘the laughing muscle’.
cards.origin: Parotid fascia and fascia over masseter
cards.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth
actions: Retracts the angle of the mouth laterally (grin, grimace)
cards.tip: Pulls the mouth corner straight sideways — more grimace than true smile.

cards.name: Rotatores
cards.etymology: From Latin rotator ‘one who turns’ (rotare, to turn, from rota, wheel), plural rotatores. So it means ‘the rotators’ — named for their assumed role in turning the spine.
cards.origin: Transverse processes of vertebrae (best developed in thoracic region)
cards.insertion: Lamina and base of spinous process 1 segment above (brevis) or 2 segments above (longus)
cards.innervation: Medial branches of dorsal rami of spinal nerves
cards.tip: The deepest, shortest transversospinalis layer — rich in muscle spindles, so likely more a position sensor than a rotator.

cards.name: Spinalis capitis
cards.etymology: From Latin spinalis ‘of the spine / spinous processes’ + capitis ‘of the head’. So it means ‘the spinous-process muscle that reaches the head’.
cards.origin: Spinous processes of C7–T1 (variable; usually arises with semispinalis capitis)
cards.insertion: Occipital bone between superior and inferior nuchal lines (with semispinalis capitis)
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of cervical spinal nerves
cards.tip: Usually inseparable from semispinalis capitis and often considered part of it.

cards.name: Spinalis cervicis (colli)
cards.etymology: From Latin spinalis ‘of the spine / spinous processes’ + cervicis ‘of the neck’ (colli, from collum). So it means ‘the spinous-process muscle of the neck’.
cards.origin: Lower ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes of C7–T2
cards.insertion: Spinous process of C2 (axis), sometimes C3–C4
cards.innervation: Dorsal rami of cervical spinal nerves
cards.tip: Small and inconstant — frequently absent or fused with semispinalis.

cards.name: Stylopharyngeus
cards.etymology: From Greek stylos ‘pillar’ (the styloid process) + pharynx ‘throat’. So it means ‘the styloid-to-throat muscle’.
cards.origin: Medial side of styloid process of temporal bone
cards.insertion: Posterior and superior borders of thyroid cartilage and pharyngeal wall (with palatopharyngeus)
cards.tip: The only muscle supplied by CN IX.

cards.name: Superior oblique
cards.etymology: From Latin superior ‘upper’ + obliquus ‘slanting’. So it means ‘the upper slanting muscle’ of the eye — its tendon runs obliquely back after hooking through the trochlea.
cards.origin: Body of sphenoid, superomedial to the optic canal
cards.insertion: Sclera, posterosuperolateral quadrant (tendon passes through the trochlea)
cards.tip: ‘SO4’: test by looking in (adduct) then down; CN IV palsy causes trouble going down stairs or reading, with a compensatory head tilt.

cards.name: Superior pharyngeal constrictor
cards.etymology: From Latin superior ‘upper’ + Greek pharynx ‘throat’ + Latin constrictor ‘one that draws tight’ (constringere). So it means ‘the upper throat squeezer’.
cards.origin: Pterygoid hamulus, pterygomandibular raphe, posterior mylohyoid line of mandible, side of tongue
cards.insertion: Pharyngeal tubercle of occipital bone and median pharyngeal raphe
cards.innervation: Vagus nerve (CN X) via pharyngeal plexus
cards.tip: Shares the pterygomandibular raphe with buccinator — the cheek wall is continuous with the pharynx wall.

cards.name: Superior rectus
cards.etymology: From Latin superior ‘upper’ + rectus ‘straight’. So it means ‘the upper straight muscle’ of the eye.
cards.origin: Common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn)
cards.insertion: Superior sclera, anterior to the equator of the eyeball
cards.tip: Test in the H-pattern: look out (abduct) then up — elevation is purely superior rectus in abduction.

cards.name: Temporoparietalis
cards.etymology: From Latin tempora ‘temples’ + paries, parietis ‘wall’ (the parietal bone). So it means ‘the temple-and-parietal muscle’ — a thin sheet over the side of the skull.
cards.origin: Temporal fascia above and in front of the ear
cards.insertion: Lateral border of epicranial aponeurosis
cards.tip: A variable, thin scalp muscle — often absent or blended with the auricular muscles.

cards.name: Thyro-arytenoid
cards.etymology: From Greek thyreoeidēs ‘shield-shaped’ (thyroid cartilage) + arytaina ‘ladle’ + eidos ‘form’ (arytenoid). So it means ‘the shield-to-ladle muscle’.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of thyroid cartilage near the midline (angle)
cards.insertion: Anterolateral surface and vocal process of arytenoid; thyro-epiglottic fibres to the aryepiglottic fold and epiglottis
actions: Relaxes and shortens the vocal folds (lowers pitch)
Thyro-epiglottic part widens the laryngeal inlet
cards.tip: Its deepest medial fibres form the vocalis, which fine-tunes vocal-fold tension.

cards.name: Transverse arytenoid
cards.etymology: From Latin transversus ‘lying across’ + Greek arytaina ‘ladle’ + eidos ‘form’ (arytenoid). So it means ‘the muscle lying across the ladle-shaped cartilages’.
cards.origin: Posterior surface of one arytenoid cartilage
cards.insertion: Posterior surface of the opposite arytenoid cartilage
actions: Draws the arytenoids together, closing the posterior (intercartilaginous) rima glottidis
cards.tip: The only unpaired intrinsic laryngeal muscle.

cards.name: Zygomaticus minor
cards.etymology: From Greek zygon ‘yoke’ (zygomatic bone) + Latin minor ‘smaller’. So it means ‘the smaller cheekbone muscle’.
cards.origin: Anterior surface of zygomatic bone
cards.insertion: Lateral part of the upper lip
cards.innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), zygomatic and buccal branches
cards.tip: Inserts into the lip, not the mouth corner — it lifts the lip to show the upper teeth.
